note: Chrome/Chromium export with every adversarial field shape.
Bitwarden export re-imported to Bitwarden: the identity case. Any mangling here is unambiguous, because input and output share a schema.
LastPass export. Note `extra` is the notes column and `name` is NOT first.
1Password 8 export. Capitalised headers: a case-sensitive matcher fails this.
CRLF line endings (a Windows export). Must parse identically to chrome_hard.
UTF-8 BOM. A BOM glued to the first header breaks naive header matching, so the format is silently mis-detected or the first column is lost.
Valid header, zero rows. Must report 0 entries explicitly, not fail and not silently emit a header-only file as if it had worked.
Zero bytes. No format can be detected, so this must be a named refusal.
Only blank lines. Must refuse, not crash and not report a phantom entry.

KeePass export -- a REAL fifth format, deliberately unsupported. The page must refuse by name and emit NO output. If a checker finds this mishandled the answer is a better refusal, never a fifth parser.
JSON with a .csv extension. Extension is not a format check.
Well-formed CSV whose headers match no supported format. Must refuse rather than guess a mapping -- a wrong guess on a password file is the worst outcome here.
5000 rows. Guards against a page that works on 7 rows and wedges the browser on a real export.
